trust_decision.summary: Caller-supplied or parsed-and-decoded attachment names are trusted to contain no CR/LF when they are put into composed header values (Content-Type name=, Content-Disposition filename=, uuencode filename); this is decided in MultipartHelper::createAndAddPartForAttachment for the build path and in the header-part decoders (MimeToken, ParameterPart) for the parse path.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'attachment filename'. Message::addAttachmentPart forwards to createAndAddPartForAttachment, which interpolates $safe into the name= and filename= header values at lines 321-322 with no CR/LF filtering.

fix_sites.entry_point: parse path: MailMimeParser parse -> IMessagePart::getFilename / getHeaderParameter on RFC 2231 name*= / filename*= (src/Message/MimePart.php:58-68); also inherited by SplitParameterPart continuations (src/Header/Part/SplitParameterPart.php:97)
fix_sites.module_kind: header parser / decoder (lower layer, parse side)

fix_sites.entry_point: parse path: any header value with an RFC 2047 encoded-word read through IHeader::getValue / getHeaderParameter (also reached from SplitParameterPart::getMimeTokens, src/Header/Part/SplitParameterPart.php:58)
fix_sites.module_kind: header token decoder (lower layer, parse side)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/Header/Part/ParameterPart.php:65-71 and src/Header/Part/MimeToken.php:46. A parsed header's decoded value (%0D%0A or an encoded-word) comes back with CR/LF and is re-emitted, e.g. src/Message/Helper/PrivacyHelper.php:84-87 (decoded protocol param -> raw Content-Type) and src/Stream/MessagePartStream.php:161 (decoded filename -> uuencode begin line)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the filename we write when adding an attachment, and the parser only reads messages. A decoded getValue() is meant to return the true decoded text, so stripping CR/LF there looks like changing parser semantics rather than fixing header building.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Composed headers must keep their own CRLF+TAB folding ("$mimeType;\r\n\tname=..."). Parsed folded headers must still unfold (CRLF+WSP is dropped, a bare CRLF becomes a space). Non-ASCII filenames must still be transliterated, not dropped. A fix that strips CR/LF inside setRawHeader or rejects the whole value breaks all of these.

O6_input_shapes: raw CR/LF in a caller-supplied filename (fix.diff:186-187)
other C0 control characters and DEL in the filename, replaced with a space (fix.diff:187)
RFC 2047 encoded-word (B or Q) whose decoded text contains CR/LF (fix.diff:153-154)
RFC 2231 percent-encoded parameter (name*=charset''..%0D%0A..), with or without charset (fix.diff:170-173)
RFC 2231 split continuations (name*0*=, name*1*=), covered by inheritance through SplitParameterPart::getValueFromParts calling decodePartValue (src/Header/Part/SplitParameterPart.php:97)
non-MIME message: the same $safe goes to UUEncodedPart::setFilename (src/Message/Helper/MultipartHelper.php:325)

O7_producer.where: src/Header/Part/ParameterPart.php:65-71 and src/Header/Part/MimeToken.php:59-87 (decoders that produce the decoded header value later re-emitted)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The attachment $mimeType (and $encoding) is put raw into Content-Type / Content-Transfer-Encoding next to the sanitized filename; only the disposition is normalized.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The MIME type is a developer-chosen constant, not user data, and the advisory names only the filename. Disposition is already normalized at src/Message.php:266.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: UUEncodedPart::setFilename is a public API that stores the filename with no CR/LF filtering; on output it goes to the uuencode 'begin' line through StreamFactory -> UUStream::setFilename.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: uuencode is a legacy non-MIME path, the begin line is written by the external zbateson/stream-decorators package, and it is not a MIME header.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 2 files from the landing point (src/Message/UUEncodedPart.php, src/Stream/StreamFactory.php:149-153); the writer is in another package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A parsed uuencode 'begin' line filename keeps a bare CR, because fgets splits only on LF and '.' matches CR. It is later re-emitted in the begin line.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A bare CR is not a line terminator in a uuencode body; legacy parser path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other package (Parser) from the landing point (Message/Helper)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: setTextPart/setHtmlPart put the caller's $charset raw into the Content-Type charset= parameter.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Charset is developer configuration, not attachment data; a neighbouring feature.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: setAsMultipartSigned puts the caller's $micalg and $protocol raw into the Content-Type header.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Signing is a separate feature with developer-supplied algorithm names; not about attachments.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'rename attachment' setter that rebuilds Content-Disposition from a new or decoded filename, alongside getFilename.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getFilename already exists, there is no setter, and a maintainer could add one using the same "$disposition;\r\n\tfilename=\"$name\"" idiom as MultipartHelper.php:322.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A helper that copies a decoded parameter (getHeaderParameter) into a new raw header, as setSignature already does with 'protocol'.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pattern already exists in the tree. A similar copy of a decoded filename/name param, e.g. when moving content in GenericHelper, is a natural addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A decoding step for quoted-string parameter values (backslash-unescape) that creates CR/LF after the Token-level stripping.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class docs say CR/LF are stripped, but decoding happens in subclasses. A new decoder added after Token::__construct would repeat the exact ordering bug the fix closes in MimeToken (strip before decode).

O9_family: CWE-93 CRLF / header injection (MIME header composition from decoded or caller-supplied values)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP >= 8.0, composer, phpunit ^9.6 (composer.json:21-34); deps guzzlehttp/psr7, zbateson/mb-wrapper, zbateson/stream-decorators, php-di
O10_build.project_tests: tests/MailMimeParser/Header/Part/MimeTokenTest.php, tests/MailMimeParser/Header/Part/ParameterPartTest.php, tests/MailMimeParser/Message/Helper/MultipartHelperTest.php (unit tests with mocks), plus integration tests under tests/

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip \r\n from $filename in createAndAddPartForAttachment only, and leave the parser decoders (which strip CR/LF before decoding, MimeToken.php:46) and the mimeType/uuencode routes untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The sanitized $safe is still placed inside a quoted-string without escaping '"' or ';' (src/Message/Helper/MultipartHelper.php:321-322), so parameters can be injected; this is not CRLF and not pursued.
IMimePart::setRawHeader / addRawHeader (src/Message/MimePart.php:270-282) take raw values by design; not treated as a route.
